summary: San Dimas Peak lookout (1917) burned in 1919; the 1930s cabin from Johnstone Peak was moved in 1992 to the LA County Fairplex, Pomona, and is on display there.

facts.design: California Region 5 Plan BC-301 cabin on a 30 ft K-brace steel tower (original site); current tower shortened with a smaller cab, painted green
facts.status_note: Relocated from Johnstone Peak in 1992 to the Los Angeles County Fairplex, Pomona; reconstructed and shortened; on display as an interpretive site.

staffing.status: last fire lookout observer in the 1950s; tower closed 1955 and decommissioned because of smog; volunteers operate it during the Los Angeles County Fair

access.note: On the Fairplex grounds in Pomona, reached from McKinley Avenue near Fairplex Drive. Volunteers operate it during the annual Los Angeles County Fair. The original summit is in the San Dimas Experimental Forest, closed to the general public except by special written permit.

facts.agency: Los Angeles County Fairplex (administers the lookout today); Angeles National Forest (original builder and site)

events.note: San Dimas Peak lookout first built, funded by the San Dimas Fruit Exchange, placed between San Dimas and Dalton Canyons.
September 1919 San Gabriel Canyon fire burned about 60,000 acres.
The fire overtook the lookout tower and completely destroyed it within a few days.
New tower built as a short open timber tower on a DuBois 4A design cab.
In August, the San Dimas observer spotted a new fire in San Gabriel Canyon that became the 1924 San Gabriel Fire.
Historical marker says the tower stood on Johnstone Peak from 1934 to 1992. Conflicts with the NHLR 1939 build date.
NHLR says the Angeles National Forest built the Plan BC-301 cabin on a 30 ft K-brace tower in 1939. Angeles Adventures says the 1930s tower was renovated or replaced.
Summit renamed Johnstone Peak in June 1940 in memory of W.A. Johnstone (died 1937); formerly San Dimas Peak Lookout.
Photo caption: Johnstone Fire Lookout, 1953, with Sandy DeLapp.
Photo caption says the lookout closed in 1955. Sandy DeLapp was the last observer, and the tower was decommissioned because of smog pollution.
Dismantled and reconstructed at the Los Angeles County Fairplex in Pomona in 1992 (NHLR). Angeles Adventures says it was moved in the early 1990s and then shortened.
Date registered November 2, 2019; nominated by Brad Eells; US 1379, CA 202.

corrections.why: The record's event list has no relocation date and the note says 'None relocated' while describing a move. NHLR says the cabin was dismantled and reconstructed at the Fairplex in 1992. The note also spells the peak 'Johnston' in one place.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 1939 for the Angeles National Forest cabin. The historical marker says the tower stood from 1934 to 1992. Angeles Adventures says the 1930s tower was renovated or replaced after a 1917 tower burned in 1919. The record keeps the NHLR 1939 date and reports the others.

NHLR describes the cabin on a 30 ft K-brace tower. Angeles Adventures says the current tower has been shortened with a smaller cab. The story reports the current tower as shorter, per Angeles Adventures.

notes_for_editor: Brief checked: 1939 build date and 2019 NHLR registration confirmed on the NHLR page; elevation 310.9 m matches the NHLR's 1,020 ft for the Fairplex site. Coordinates and elevation in the record are for the Fairplex display site; the original summit is a separate site (NHLR gives 34.160096, -117.799767 for the original location, not read in this pass beyond the NHLR snippet) and the sibling record us-ca-johnstone-peak-san-dimas covers it. The build date conflicts across sources (1934 marker, 1939 NHLR, 1930s Angeles Adventures) and is reported as a conflict. Staffing after 1958 and fire history are thin; the 1919 and 1924 fire items come from Angeles Adventures and the San Dimas page's newspaper clippings. Photos on Angeles Adventures (credit Ron Kemnow 2009, Mike Guerin) were not added because licences were not checked. The volunteer groups are named on the NHLR page itself (read 2026-10-08). Not verified: any separate Southern California Mountains Foundation post (search snippet only, not read) or the Forest Lookout Association list.
